tagline: Coordinate billing feature releases with Stripe configuration and catch payment-related code risks before they ship
metaTitle: GitHub + Stripe Integration: Payment Code Review Alerts
metaDescription: Flag PRs that touch payment code and open GitHub issues from Stripe webhook failures. GAIA checks billing releases. See the setup steps.
intro:
Payment engineering is high stakes—a breaking change to payment integration code or a billing feature shipped without coordinated product configuration can result in failed charges, broken checkouts, and revenue loss. Yet many engineering teams manage their GitHub and Stripe workflows in complete isolation, without guardrails that catch dangerous coordination errors before they reach production.

GAIA connects the two to add safety and coordination to payment engineering workflows. When a PR touches Stripe-related files, GAIA automatically flags it for extra review scrutiny and checks against current API versions. When a billing feature is deployed via a GitHub release, GAIA can verify that the corresponding product or price configuration has been updated before the release goes live.

For SaaS engineering teams, this integration provides the coordination layer between code deployments and billing infrastructure that currently relies on manual checklists and Slack reminders, replacing tribal knowledge with automated guardrails.

useCases.title: Flag PRs that touch payment code for extra review
useCases.description: When a pull request modifies files in payment-related directories or imports Stripe libraries, GAIA automatically adds a payment-sensitive label and assigns a designated payments reviewer, ensuring no billing change ships without proper scrutiny.

useCases.title: Verify payment config before billing feature releases
useCases.description: Before a GitHub release that includes billing changes goes live, GAIA checks that the required products, prices, and webhook endpoints are configured correctly in the target environment, alerting the team to any discrepancies.

useCases.title: Create GitHub issues from Stripe webhook failures
useCases.description: When webhook deliveries start failing, GAIA creates an issue in the relevant repository with the error details and a link to the dashboard, automatically assigning it to the payments team.

useCases.title: Track Stripe API version upgrades as GitHub issues
useCases.description: When a new API version is announced, GAIA creates an issue in your billing repository with the breaking changes, migration guide link, and a suggested timeline based on the deprecation schedule.

useCases.title: Deployment rollback checklist for billing changes
useCases.description: When a release that touches billing code is deployed, GAIA creates a time-limited issue with a rollback checklist including billing-specific steps that stays open until the deployment is confirmed stable.

howItWorks.step: Connect GitHub and Stripe to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authenticate your repositories and account in GAIA's settings. GAIA uses restricted API keys with read-only access to the product catalog and webhook configuration.
Configure which directories or files are considered payment-sensitive, who the required reviewers are, what pre-release checks to run, and how to handle webhook failure alerts.

howItWorks.step: GAIA enforces payment engineering guardrails automatically
howItWorks.description: GAIA monitors both sides for relevant events and enforces the rules you've defined, creating issues, alerting reviewers, or notifying on-call as configured without manual intervention.

faqs.question: Can GAIA prevent a GitHub release from deploying if Stripe config is wrong?
faqs.answer: GAIA can block a deployment step in an Actions workflow by failing a pre-deployment check and posting the configuration discrepancies as a PR comment. Actual deployment gating requires integrating GAIA's check into your CI/CD pipeline.

faqs.question: Does GAIA need full access to the payment account?
faqs.answer: No. GAIA uses restricted API keys with read-only access to products, prices, and webhook endpoints. GAIA never needs access to customer payment data or live charge records.

faqs.question: Can GAIA help us track which API version we're on?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA can scan your codebase for the API version pinned in your configuration files and compare it against the current API version, creating an issue when you're running behind on upgrades.

faqs.question: Does this work for both test mode and live mode?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA can be configured to monitor your test environment for staging deployments and your live environment for production releases, with separate alerting thresholds for each.
